literature.headline_zh: 马尔堡病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期马尔堡病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 分子对接研究揭示了 疫苗 和免疫受体之间存在强大而稳定的相互作用,正如良好的 HDOCK 评分 (− 315.21) 和高置信度值 (0.9646) 所反映的那样。通过 iMODS 进行的正态模式分析证明了适当的分子灵活性,低特征值 (3.61×10–6) 表明了这一点。免疫模拟显示出强烈的体液和细胞 免疫应答,其特征是 IgG 和 IgM 水平增加、细胞因子分泌(IFN-γ、IL-2、TNF-α)以及记忆细胞的发育。 [10.1007/s13337-026-00987-5]
我们的数据表明,可以使用大肠杆菌表达系统以低成本生产三种重组 S-GP 蛋白 S-GP278、S-GP377 和 S-GP486。纯化的重组S-GP蛋白高效自组装成PVNP。 [10.3390/pathogens15101087]
对于所有时间和正初始条件,模型具有非负解。建立了模型的不变区域,揭示了种群规模是有界的。敏感性分析表明,接触率、有效接触概率和暴露者感染率具有正敏感性指数,而暴露人群和传染人群的隔离率、死亡率以及暴露人群和传染人群的治愈率具有负敏感性指数。 [10.33003/fjs-2026-1020-5893]
数据中出现的主题包括影响就医行为的因素、经济限制、“同一个健康”的重要性、部门间合作薄弱以及导致 疫苗 拒绝的错误信息。 [10.1186/s12889-026-29896-4]

papers.full_text: Abstract Marburg virus (MARV) is an extremely virulent pathogen for which effective preventive and therapeutic strategis remain limited, highlighting the urgent demand for a safe and efficient vaccine. In this study, an immunoinformatics-based approach was employed to design a novel multi-epitope subunit vaccine capable of eliciting robust humoral and cell mediated immune responses. Highly conserved cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were systematically predicted and assembled using GGGS, GPGPG and KK linkers respectively. To enhance immunogenicity, the construct was fused with the 50S ribosomal protein L7/L12 as an adjuvant, while a PADRE sequence was incorporated to promote broad CD4+ T-cell activation across diverse HLA alleles. The three-dimensional structure of the vaccine construct was modelled, refined and evaluated for stability and structural integrity using validation tools including ERRAT, Ramachandran plot analysis, MolProbity scoring, and RMSD assessment. Molecular docking studies revealed strong and stable interactions between the vaccine and immune receptors, as reflected by a favourable HDOCK score (− 315.21) and a high confidence value (0.9646). Additionally, normal mode analysis conducted via iMODS demonstrated appropriate molecular flexibility, indicated by a low eigen value (3.61×10–6), supporting effective receptor engagement and immune activation. Immune simulations revealed strong humoral and cellular immune responses, marked by increased levels of IgG and IgM, cytokine secretion (IFN-γ, IL-2, TNF-α), and the development of memory cells. The optimized gene attained a Codon Adaptation Index (CAI) of 1.0 along with a GC content of 54.49%, indicating its appropriateness for expression in Escherichia coli utilizing the pET-28a( +) vector. In summary, the Insilico results present the constructed vaccine as a promising multi-epitope candidate against the Marburg virus, necessitating additional experimental tests to validate its immunogenic effectiveness and protective capability. papers.title: Modeling the Dynamics of the Marburg Virus Disease
papers.abstract: This work models the infection dynamics of the Marburg Virus Disease using the SEIQR model. It is a five-compartment model. We investigated the non-negativity of solutions, invariant region and boundedness, equilibrium points, basic reproduction number, sensitivity, equilibrium points’ stability, and bifurcation of the model. For all time and positive initial conditions, we observed that the model has non-negative solutions. The invariant region of the model is established, revealing the population size is bounded. The sensitivity analysis shows that the contact rate, the probability of effective contact and the rate at which exposed individuals become infectious have positive sensitivity indices, while the quarantine rates for the exposed and infectious classes, the death rates, and the recovery rates for the exposed and infectious classes have negative sensitivity indices. We established that the non-negativity of the residual vector , resulting from the difference between the rate of change of infected individuals and the Metzler matrix, stops the existence of several endemic equilibria for . Thus, no critical value exists, and there is an extension of local stability of the disease-free equilibrium to global stability on the entire domain. The bifurcation analysis reveals a forward bifurcation and the bifurcation plot confirms that for effective management and eradication the disease, the basic reproduction number must satisfy , where is a critical value. The mathematical analysis also reveals that the disease-free equilibrium is globally asymptotically stable. The effects of some sensitive parameters on the infectious class are shown via numerical simulations.

papers.title: Pseudovirus Nanoparticles Displaying the Receptor-Binding Glycoprotein of Marburg Virus as Potential Vaccine Candidates
papers.abstract: Background: The lack of a licensed vaccine against the deadly Marburg virus (MARV) calls for the development of a novel and effective vaccine strategy. Methods: We report here our development of three pseudovirus nanoparticles (PVNPs), each displaying a MARV-neutralizing glycoprotein (GP) segment of different lengths, as MARV vaccine candidates. These PVNPs, designated S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, were generated using our proprietary norovirus shell nanoparticle (SNP) platform. The PVNPs were evaluated for their production, self-assembly, morphology, structural properties, and immunogenicity. Results: Our data demonstrated that the three recombinant S-GP proteins, S-GP278, S-GP377, and S-GP486, can be produced at low cost using an E. coli expression system. The purified recombinant S-GP proteins self-assembled into PVNPs with high efficacy. Structural modeling of the S-GP1 PVNPs highlighted their key architectural features, consisting of an icosahedral inner shell and multiple trimeric GP structures displayed on the surface. Immunization of mice with the S-GP PVNPs elicited high titers of GP-specific antibodies, including IgG and IgA. Conclusions: Collectively, these data support the notion that the S-GP PVNPs may serve as potential MARV vaccine candidates worthy of further development.

papers.title: Community barriers, perceptions, and health-seeking behaviors within the one health approach in six priority districts of Rwanda: a descriptive qualitative study
papers.abstract: Rwanda’s health security can only be strengthened through integrated One Health approaches that link human, animal, and environmental health. Emerging health threats such as the Marburg Virus highlight the urgency, yet fragmented systems, weak coordination, and behavioral barriers continue to constrain resilience. Thus, we assessed behavioral, social, and systemic determinants influencing community resilience, outbreak preparedness, and response, using the Health Belief Model (HBM) and the Social Ecological Model (SEM) to generate actionable evidence for strengthening One Health integration, health system performance, and risk communication strategies for effective disease prevention and outbreak mitigation in Rwanda. Our descriptive qualitative assessment included participants from Rulindo, Kayonza, Nyanza, Rusizi, Rubavu, and Nyaruguru districts of Rwanda. We had six In-depth Interviews (IDIs) per district and two Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) per district. ST PHOTO: CHONG JUN LIANG Yap Wei Qiang Published Oct 19, 2026, 05:00 AM Updated Oct 19, 2026, 07:23 AM Set as preferred source Listen SINGAPORE – Singapore has stepped up surveillance of three potentially deadly diseases that have no approved vaccines or antiviral treatments, with medical practitioners required to report all cases to the authorities from Oct 31. These diseases are Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever (CCHF), Lassa fever and Marburg virus disease (MVD). The Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) said it has been monitoring them for some time “as all three diseases are viral haemorrhagic fevers that can cause severe illness and have the potential for human-to-human transmission”. The diseases could have fatality rates of up to 50%, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). They will be added to the Infectious Diseases Act’s (IDA) list of infectious diseases, following the amendment of IDA and its related regulations in September by the Ministry of Health (MOH). This means that all medical practitioners such as doctors, as well as clinical laboratories, are legally required to notify the authorities of all confirmed as well as suspected cases. Although the risk posed by these diseases to Singapore remains low, the latest moves will ensure the nation is prepared to respond when necessary, said a CDA spokeswoman in response to queries from The Straits Times. The notification of cases will support early detection and a timely public health response, which could include measures such as isolation of cases and activation of contact tracing, she added. The WHO website states that there is currently no specific treatment or vaccine approved for any of the diseases, though there is ongoing vaccine development for Lassa fever and MVD. Diseases with high fatality rates The WHO information showed that fatality rates of the three diseases could go as high as 50%. CCHF can cause severe viral haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, with a fatality rate of up to 40%. It is transmitted primarily through tick bites, contact with infected livestock, as well as close contact with the blood, secretions or other bodily fluids of infected people. There is sudden onset of symptoms, such as fever, muscle ache, dizziness, sore eyes and photophobia (sensitivity to light), as well as sharp mood swings and confusion. Severely ill patients may experience rapid kidney deterioration, sudden liver failure or pulmonary failure. Lassa fever has an overall fatality rate of 1%, rising to at least 15% for those hospitalised with severe illness. It is more concerning for pregnant women as foetal death rates can go beyond 80% in the third trimester and maternal death rates can exceed 30%. The virus is mainly transmitted through food or items contaminated with rodent urine or faeces, and possibly human to human. About 80% of those infected have no or mild symptoms such as sore throat, muscle pain, nausea, vomiting and diarrhoea. Severe cases may suffer from facial swelling, fluid in the lung cavity, bleeding from the mouth, nose, vagina or gastrointestinal tract, and low blood pressure. Even after recovery, up to 25% of patients reported sudden hearing loss, and most of them never regained their hearing. More on this topic Risk of another pandemic crisis remains, Ong Ye Kung tells attendees at Geneva event New infectious diseases agency to chart S'pore’s new pandemic plans: PM Wong As for MVD, the virus is transmitted by a type of fruit bat known as rousettus aegyptiacus or between people, and the average fatality rate is around 50%, said WHO. Symptoms include sudden onset of high fever, severe headache, and muscle aches and pains. Some may experience bleeding from the nose, gums and vagina, as well as confusion, irritability and aggression. The CDA spokeswoman said: “While there has been no change to the risk level from these three diseases, which currently remains low, they have been added to the IDA to strengthen our overall surveillance and preparedness efforts.” She reiterated that CDA continuously monitors the global and local infectious disease situation, so as to detect and respond to infectious disease threats early. “As part of our preparedness efforts, CDA periodically reviews and updates the list of infectious diseases under the IDA to ensure that Singapore remains ready to respond to infectious disease risks,” she said. Asked whether Singapore’s current border control measures could keep these diseases at bay, she said the measures already cover detection. These measures include the Electronic Health Declaration card, which requires incoming travellers, including returning residents, to declare their health status and travel history. Medical assessment is also available at points of entry for travellers who show symptoms and have travelled to specific affected areas. Number of dangerous infectious diseases rises to 8 The various legislative amendments made by MOH included amending the Second Schedule of the IDA, which pertains to the list of “dangerous infectious diseases”. With the addition of the three diseases, the list will grow to a total of eight diseases. The five dangerous diseases currently listed are Ebola, the Middle East respiratory syndrome coronavirus infection (MERS-CoV), plague, severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) and yellow fever. CDA said its weekly bulletin will include the three newly listed diseases from November. The bulletin reports the number of new cases and polyclinic attendances for various infectious diseases in Singapore. The previous amendment to the Second Schedule was in 2024, when Covid-19 was delisted as a dangerous infectious disease. news.content: Close Menu Facebook X (Twitter) Instagram Facebook Instagram Threads Subscribe Featured Ebola Outbreak Avian Influenza Measles Resurgence Vaccine News Events Advertisement Medical Countermeasures UK Commits £33.2 Million to Eight Vaccine Projects Targeting Ebola, Marburg, Plague and Other Epidemic Threats Funding through the UK Vaccine Network aims to speed development and deployment of vaccines for diseases with epidemic potential, with a focus on low- and middle-income countries By Global Biodefense StaffOctober 18, 2026 Background of compilation image credit: Shutterstock, modified Share Facebook LinkedIn Reddit Email The UK government has announced £33.2 million to fund eight vaccine projects against some of the world’s deadliest infectious diseases. The awards, announced October 8, 2026 by the Department of Health and Social Care, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and Innovate UK, target Ebola, plague, Marburg virus, Lassa fever, Nipah virus, chikungunya and Mayaro virus. The money will advance promising vaccine candidates, clinical trials and technologies intended to make vaccine design and manufacture faster. It will also build the research, clinical trial and technical capacity needed to develop, test and deploy vaccines quickly when a new threat emerges, and to make those vaccines affordable and accessible in the countries at greatest risk. Richard Pebody, UKHSA’s Director of Epidemic and Emerging Infections, cited the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as a reminder that emerging diseases “are not a distant threat,” and said effective vaccines and the manufacturing capability to produce them at speed are essential alongside detection and response. The announcement also referenced a suspected pneumonic plague case linked to a laboratory worker’s death in Russia’s Irkutsk region, with nearly 200 contacts placed under precautionary medical observation, as another sign that serious infectious disease risks persist. The awards are delivered through the UK Vaccine Network, an expert advisory group which brings together industry, academia and funders to guide government investment. Its premise is a market failure: outbreaks of some of the deadliest diseases occur intermittently and often in poor countries, so there is little commercial incentive for industry to develop vaccines against them. The UK committed £134 million to its first phase between 2016 and 2022, with further investment committed for 2023 to 2029. Government officials note the programme previously supported development of the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine. The network maintains a priority pathogen list covering 12 families of viruses and bacteria, including Lassa fever virus, MERS, Marburg and Sudan ebolavirus, Nipah virus, Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever, Rift Valley fever, chikungunya, Q fever and plague. It will not fund work on pathogens that already have licensed vaccines or advanced candidates, nor on SARS-CoV-2 or influenza. It also supports vaccine technology development suited to responding to novel pathogens, the so-called “disease X” scenario. Health Minister Chris McDonald said investing before a crisis hits helps protect the public and ensure the UK is ready to respond to future threats. Whitty said the aim is to prevent some of the most dangerous infectious diseases in the world today.
